senses.gloss: m.(b. h.; קָוַץ or קוּץ I)thorn.
units: <cite ref="Rosh Hashanah 17a:1">R. Hash. 17ᵃ</cite> bot. (ref. to <cite ref="Micah 7:18">Mic. VII, 18</cite>) <he>אליה וק׳ בה וכ׳</he> a fat tail with a thorn in it (a consolation implying an evil prediction), ‘to the remnant of his inheritance’ (pardon will be granted), but not to his entire inheritance.
<cite ref="Bereishit Rabbah 20:10">Gen. R. s. 20</cite> [read:] <he>ק׳ זה קינרס</he> by ‘thorn’ (<cite ref="Genesis 3:18">Gen. III, 18</cite>) artichoke is meant.
<cite ref="Midrash Tehillim 136:2">Midr. Till. to Ps. CXXXVI</cite> <he>ישב לו ק׳ וכ׳</he> a thorn got into the foot of one of them (which prevented him from travelling); a. fr.—

<cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Shabbat 9:1:3">Y. Sabb. IX, 11ᵈ</cite> <he>עין כוס עין קוץ</he> if an idolatrous place is called ʿEn K’os (well of the cup) call it (cacophemistically) ʿEn Ḳots (well of the thorn); <cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Avodah Zarah 3:6:3">Y. Ab. Zar. III, 43ᵃ</cite> bot.—Pl. <he>קוֹצִים</he>, <he>קוֹצִין</he>.

<cite ref="Bereishit Rabbah 45:10">Gen. R. s. 45</cite>, v. <cite ref="N00848"><he>נָכַשׁ</he></cite>; <cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Maasrot 3:4:5">Y. Maasr. III, 50ᵈ</cite> bot., v. <cite ref="K00315"><he>כּוֹס</he> II</cite>.

<cite ref="Shemot Rabbah 1:17">Ex. R. s. 1</cite> (ref. to <he>ויקצו</he>, <cite ref="Exodus 1:12">Ex. I, 12</cite>) <he>שהיו דומין … כק׳</he> the Israelites were like thorns in their eyes; Yalk. ib. 162 <he>שהם בעיניהם כק׳</he> they (the Egyptians) were in their own eyes like thorns (dwarfed and dry plants).

<cite ref="Bamidbar Rabbah 20:25">Num. R. s. 20</cite> (ref. to <he>ויקץ</he>, <cite ref="Numbers 22:3">Num. XXII, 3</cite>) <he>שהיו … כק׳ בפניהם</he> they looked upon themselves as if they were thorns compared with them (the Israelites).

<cite ref="Kiddushin 75b:8">Kidd. 75ᵇ</cite> (play on <he>מקצותם</he>, <cite ref="II Kings 17:32">II Kings XVII, 32</cite>) <he>מן הק׳ שבעם</he> from the thorns (the basest) of the people, opp. <he>הבחירים</he>; Y. Ab. Zar. I, beg. 39ᵃ.

<cite ref="Bava Metzia 83a:1">B. Mets. 83ᵃ</cite> <he>ק׳ … מן הכרם</he> (in serving the Roman government as an executioner) I only destroy the thorns out of the vineyard; <he>יבא … את קוֹצָיו</he> let the owner of the vineyard (God) come and destroy his thorns; <cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Maasrot 3:4:5">Y. Maasr. III, 50ᵈ</cite> bot.; (Pesik. B’shall., p. 92ᵃ <he>כוסים וכ׳</he>), v. <cite ref="K00913"><he>כָּסח</he></cite>; a. fr.—
<cite ref="Shir HaShirim Rabbah 5:11:2">Cant. R. to V, 11</cite>, v. infra.—
Midr. Till. to Ps. XIV בתי ק׳ (cacophem.) idolatrous temples (v. supra); Yalk. Ps. 662.—2) (also קוֹצָה f.) prick, stroke on letters, apex. Tanḥ.
<cite ref="Genesis 1:1">B’resh. 1</cite>; <cite ref="Menachot 29b:3">Men. 29ᵇ</cite> <he>לדרוש על כל ק׳ וק׳ וכ׳</he> to teach mounds of rules on every tip (of letters in the Torah).
Ib.ᵃ קוֹצוֹ של יו״ד Ms. M. a. Rashi (ed. קוצה) the prick on the top of the letter Yod (Rashi: the foot of Yod); ib. 34ᵃ.

<cite ref="Shemot Rabbah 6:5">Ex. R. s. 6</cite>, beg. <he>שלמה … וקוצה ממך וכ׳</he> Solomon and a thousand like him shall pass away, but not a tittle of thee (the Torah) will I allow to be expunged; a. e.—Pl. as ab.
<cite ref="Vayikra Rabbah 19:6">Lev. R. s. 19</cite> (ref. to <he>קוצותיו</he>, <cite ref="Song of Songs 5:11">Cant. V, 11</cite>) <he>אלו קוֹצֵי האותיות</he> this means the strokes of the letters.

<cite ref="Song of Songs 5:11">Ib.</cite> <he>אפי׳ דברים … שהן ק׳ וכ׳</he> even things which you consider to be merely strokes (ornamentations of letters), in the Torah they are mounds upon mounds (v. supra); <cite ref="Shir HaShirim Rabbah 5:11:6">Cant. R. to V, 11</cite> <he>בתורה הן קוצי ק׳</he> in the Torah these strokes are thorns of thorns (intimating thorny problems).
